Tap the button below and turn on “Sidepeek” in the list. You’ll move to the next step automatically when you come back.
Notification access: is the switch greyed out?
Phones like ASUS and Pixel block apps not installed from a store: the switch is grey, or “App was denied access” appears.
" Tap “Close” first, then tap “Unlock in App info” below → ⋮ at the top right → “Allow restricted settings”, verify, come back and turn on notification access."
\n\nWhile in App info, also turn off “Pause app activity if unused”, so permissions aren’t removed if you don’t open the app for a long time.
\nIf you just haven’t turned it on yet, tap “Open notification access settings”.
Allowed, but not connected yet. Tap Reconnect; if that doesn’t help, turn “Sidepeek” off and on again in the list.
Lets “Sidepeek” post the organized notifications. Just tap Allow below.

A translucent “Peek bar” appears at the screen edge; swipe in from it to read messages (much like Samsung’s Edge panel handle). The next steps help you turn on the service. If now isn’t a good time, tap “Set up the side panel later”; notification organizing works either way.
Tap “Installed apps” → “Sidepeek side panel” → turn it on. If a “denied” window appears, tap Close, then tap Next below.
" (Only turn on the service switch. The “shortcut” below isn’t needed; it adds a floating button to the screen.)"
I closed the denied window, next
Now ⋮ appears at the top right. Tap ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then come back.
Turn on the side panel service again
Go back to Accessibility → Installed apps → “Sidepeek side panel” → turn it on. You’ll move to the next step automatically.
" (The “shortcut” below isn’t needed; it adds a floating button to the screen.)"
Battery saving may close “Sidepeek” and you’d miss messages. Tap below and allow “Unrestricted”.
\nOption names may differ a little between system versions. When done, tap “I’ve set it up, next”.
All required settings are done. Day to day you only need the main switch at the top of Home; everything else is in the Settings tab below.
⚠️ On a call: to prevent scams, Android doesn’t allow turning on accessibility services or restricted settings during a call.
" Please hang up and continue, or tap “Set up the side panel later” below.\n\n"

OK. You can continue side panel setup later from “Continue side panel setup” at the top.

Tap ⋮ at the top right → Allow restricted settings, then come back and turn on the side panel service

Set this category to Silent (no sound, no pop-up). Don’t turn it off completely.

Please open it yourself: Settings → Apps → Sidepeek → Battery
The service is called “Sidepeek side panel”. It’s only for the side panel; notification organizing works without it.
Which app is in front (its package name), and whether you’re on the home screen.
Whether a keyboard window is on screen.
The Back key you press while the side panel is open.
Showing the Peek bar at the screen edge and opening the side panel when you swipe in (no persistent notification needed).
Deciding whether the Peek bar shows, e.g. “Show only on home screen” or hiding it while typing.
Closing the side panel with the Back key.
Clearing the LINE notifications Sidepeek organized when you open LINE (by default nothing on LINE’s screen is read).
Never reads, stores or sends any text or content on the screen. The only exception is if you separately turn on “Advanced clearing” (off by default; you’ll be asked to agree when turning it on).
Never taps or operates any app for you.
All of the above is used on the phone in real time only: not logged, not uploaded, not shared with anyone.
Go to Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Sidepeek side panel and turn it off.
Advanced clearing reads text on LINE’s screen
This is an experimental feature, off by default. When on, Sidepeek uses the “Sidepeek side panel” service to read the text in the title bar at the top of LINE’s screen.
Only inside LINE, and only the title bar at the very top (the row with the chat name).
Never reads chat content, the input field, photos, or other apps’ screens.
Matching it with the chat names already in Sidepeek’s notifications, so only the chat you’re reading is cleared and other chats’ notifications stay.
If nothing matches, or several chats match, nothing is cleared.
The text is compared once on the phone and then discarded: never stored, uploaded or shared.
The diagnostic log normally only records “matched / not matched”. Only when you start a full log yourself is the title text written to it, to help report problems.
Turn off the “Advanced clearing” switch to stop reading; it goes back to clearing everything when you open LINE.
Before turning on the side panel
No problem: notification organizing still works. The side panel can use the “Display over other apps” fallback instead.

Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → add “Sidepeek”.
Settings → Apps → Manage apps → “Sidepeek”: turn on “Autostart” and set “Battery saver” to “No restrictions”.
Settings → Apps → App management → “Sidepeek” → Battery usage: allow “Auto launch” and “Run in background”.
Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management → “Sidepeek”: choose “Allow high background power consumption”; then in i Manager → App manager → Autostart manager, turn on “Sidepeek”.
Settings → Battery → App launch → set “Sidepeek” to Manage manually, and turn on “Auto-launch”, “Secondary launch” and “Run in background”.
